predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
predecessors.text: the Lordship of Schellenberg and the County of Vaduz, bought from the Hohenems in 1699 and 1712

ledger.x: 1719: Charles VI raises Vaduz and Schellenberg to the Principality of Liechtenstein.
March 1799: France occupies Liechtenstein in the War of the Second Coalition.
May 1799: Austrian and Vorarlberg militias under Jelacic defeat the French and liberate the country 'by 14 May'.
1949: Liechtenstein cedes the Ellhorn to Switzerland.

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.outcome: France occupied all of Liechtenstein from 6 March 1799; Austrian and Vorarlberg militias defeated the French and liberated it by 14 May 1799.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars
wars.outcome: After Austerlitz (1805) and the end of the Empire, Liechtenstein became a sovereign state in 1806 by joining Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine; the page notes that Maximilian I of Bavaria wanted to annex it in 1806, which did not happen.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prince Johann II placed soldiers at the German Confederation's disposal 'only to defend the German territory of Tyrol'; the Liechtenstein army marched home on 22 July after the war; the Confederation was dissolved in 1866 and Liechtenstein became fully…
